title: The visible and invisible scars of childhood cancer: A qualitative study of body image and identity in survivorship
titleZh: 童年癌症可见与不可见的伤痕：癌症生存者身体意象与身份认同的质性研究
abstract: Abstract Objectives This study explored the lived experiences of young adult childhood cancer survivors regarding the impact of visible physical differences on body image and identity. Although clinical survival rates have increased, the long‐term psychological implications of treatment‐related physical alterations remain under‐researched. Design A qualitative study adopting a constructivist‐interpretivist approach. Methods We conducted semi‐structured interviews with 41 survivors (aged 19–28) recruited from a Spanish paediatric oncology unit. Data were analysed using reflexive thematic analysis. Results This analysis revealed a complex trajectory of embodiment across four central themes: Permanent Body Changes and Physical Consequences ; Damage to Body Image, Self‐Perception and Identity ; Insecurity and Isolation in the Social/Sexual Sphere ; and Coping Strategies—From Hiding to Acceptance . This trajectory spans from the initial trauma of permanent physical consequences and functional limitations to a sense of “spoiled identity” characterized by body shame and social avoidance. The findings highlight how visible scars and developmental delays often disrupt socio‐sexual integration, creating a significant “disclosure burden” in romantic contexts. However, the analysis also identifies a dynamic shift towards resilience, where survivors increasingly re‐signify physical marks as symbols of strength and survival. Conclusion These results underscore the need for developmentally sensitive, lifelong psychosocial support that moves beyond biomedical metrics to address the nuanced, experiential reality of life after childhood cancer.
summaryZh: 分析归纳出四个核心主题：永久性身体改变与身体后果；身体意象、自我感知与身份认同受损；社会/性领域中的不安全感与孤立；从隐藏到接纳的应对策略。 参与者经历从永久身体后果与功能限制的初始创伤，到以身体羞耻和社会回避为特征的“受损身份”感。 可见疤痕与发育延迟常干扰社会-性整合，并在恋爱情境中形成显著的“披露负担”。 分析也识别出向韧性发展的动态转变，生存者逐渐将身体印记重新赋义为力量与生存的象征。
